---
title: "Interpolation between brain regions"
author: "[Michael Love](http://mikelove.github.io)"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
---

```{r message=FALSE}
library(here)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(magrittr)
library(matrixStats)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("bioc","my_scale_counts.R"))
```

Load and scale data.

```{r}
load(here("eda","brain.rda"))
se <- my_scale_counts(rse_gene)
cts <- assay(se)
condition <- se$smtsd
condition %<>% (function(x) sub("Brain - (.*)", "\\1", x))
condition %<>% factor
```

Filter genes with low total counts.

```{r}
cts <- cts[rowSums(cts) > 100,]
dim(cts)
```

Identify Spinal cord and Hypothalamus samples.

```{r}
sc_idx <- grep("Spinal cord", as.character(condition))
hypo_idx <- grep("Hypothalamus", as.character(condition))
cat("Spinal cord:", length(sc_idx), "  Hypothalamus:", length(hypo_idx), "\n")
```

Pick one sample from each region and create 10 pseudosamples by linear interpolation on the log count scale. A weight of 0 gives the Hypothalamus sample, weight 1 gives the Spinal cord sample.

```{r}
sc_log   <- log10(cts[, "SRR1402882"] + 1)
hypo_log <- log10(cts[, "SRR1413454"] + 1)

weights <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 10)
pseudo  <- sapply(weights, function(w) w * sc_log + (1 - w) * hypo_log)
colnames(pseudo) <- paste0("pseudo_", seq_len(10))
```

Combine with all Spinal cord and Hypothalamus samples, log-transform the real samples, and run PCA on the top 500 most variable genes.

```{r}
logcts <- cbind(log10(cts[, sc_idx] + 1), log10(cts[, hypo_idx] + 1), pseudo)
group <- c(
  rep("Spinal cord", length(sc_idx)),
  rep("Hypothalamus", length(hypo_idx)),
  rep("Pseudosample", 10)
)

rv <- rowVars(logcts)
o  <- order(rv, decreasing = TRUE)[1:500]
pc <- prcomp(t(logcts[o,]))
```

Pseudosamples are colored by interpolation weight (0 = Hypothalamus, 1 = Spinal cord). Real samples are shown as filled circles.

```{r fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
dat      <- data.frame(pc$x[, 1:2], group = group)
dat_real <- dat[dat$group != "Pseudosample",]
dat_pseudo <- dat[dat$group == "Pseudosample",]
dat_pseudo$weight <- weights

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = dat_pseudo,
             aes(PC1, PC2, color = weight), shape = 18, size = 4, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "tomato", high = "steelblue",
                       name = "interp.\nweight") +
  geom_point(data = dat_real,
             aes(PC1, PC2, fill = group), shape = 21, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Spinal cord" = "steelblue",
                               "Hypothalamus" = "tomato")) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Classify the 10 pseudosamples

Fit a regularized logistic regression to the real samples. The two samples used
to construct the pseudosamples are left out of the training data so that the
classifier does not see the exact interpolation endpoints. Gene selection and
cross-validation also use only the remaining real samples; the interpolation
weights are not supplied to the classifier.

Run `install.packages("glmnet")` once if the package is not already installed.

```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install glmnet first with install.packages('glmnet')")
}

# Assemble real samples and remove the two interpolation endpoints.
real_idx <- c(hypo_idx, sc_idx)
real_log <- log10(cts[, real_idx] + 1)
endpoint_ids <- c("SRR1402882", "SRR1413454")
train_keep <- !colnames(real_log) %in% endpoint_ids
train_log <- real_log[, train_keep, drop = FALSE]

# 1 = Spinal cord, 0 = Hypothalamus.
y <- as.integer(grepl("Spinal cord", condition[real_idx][train_keep]))

# Select features using training samples only.
train_rv <- rowVars(train_log)
feature_idx <- order(train_rv, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(500, nrow(train_log)))]
x_train <- t(train_log[feature_idx, , drop = FALSE])
x_pseudo <- t(pseudo[feature_idx, , drop = FALSE])

# Use balanced observation weights because the class sizes differ.
obs_weights <- ifelse(
  y == 1,
  length(y) / (2 * sum(y == 1)),
  length(y) / (2 * sum(y == 0))
)

# Make the same stratified folds for every alpha value.
set.seed(784)
nfolds <- 10
foldid <- integer(length(y))
for (class_value in 0:1) {
  idx <- which(y == class_value)
  foldid[idx] <- sample(rep(seq_len(nfolds), length.out = length(idx)))
}

# Cross-validation chooses both alpha and lambda.
alpha_grid <- c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
cv_fits <- lapply(alpha_grid, function(alpha_value) {
  glmnet::cv.glmnet(
    x = x_train,
    y = y,
    family = "binomial",
    alpha = alpha_value,
    weights = obs_weights,
    foldid = foldid,
    type.measure = "deviance"
  )
})

best_fit_idx <- which.min(vapply(cv_fits, function(fit) min(fit$cvm), numeric(1)))
best_fit <- cv_fits[[best_fit_idx]]
best_alpha <- alpha_grid[best_fit_idx]

# lambda.1se favors the simpler model within one standard error of the minimum.
p_spinal <- drop(predict(
  best_fit,
  newx = x_pseudo,
  s = "lambda.1se",
  type = "response"
))

classification <- data.frame(
  sample = colnames(pseudo),
  p_spinal_cord = p_spinal,
  predicted_label = ifelse(p_spinal >= 0.5, "Spinal cord", "Hypothalamus")
)

best_alpha
classification
```

The probability is a model-based continuous score: values near 0 favor
Hypothalamus, values near 1 favor Spinal cord, and values near 0.5 are
borderline. Because the pseudosamples are artificial mixtures, the probability
is more informative than pretending every sample has an unambiguous biological
identity.

```{r}
sessionInfo()
```
